claims.text: ``docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.json`` used to be typed by hand. It stamped the revision it was written against and then sat there while thirty commits landed on top of it... This module replaces the typing. It derives every mechanical field from the same single walk of the tree that ``daedalus map`` already performs (:func:`daedalus.mapping.render.analyse_once`), so the census cannot be older than the run that produced it.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the derivation logic; it only sets up constants and digest functions. The claim about deriving from analyse_once cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Derivable... the module census and its ``status`` -- wired / island / shim / unknown -- straight off :func:`daedalus.mapping.reach.analyse`'s classification;
claims.why: STATUS_BY_CLASS is defined, but the actual classification logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Derivable... ``entrypoints``, ``entry_kinds``, ``importers`` and ``tests`` per module;
claims.why: No code for these fields appears in this chunk.

claims.text: Derivable... the CLI dispatch table and the HTTP route table, from the entry points;
claims.why: No code for these tables appears in this chunk.

claims.text: Derivable... every environment switch, where it is read, whether it is dark and whether any document mentions it, from :mod:`daedalus.mapping.switches`;
claims.why: No code for environment switches appears in this chunk.

claims.text: Derivable... two kinds of ``stale``: a package this repo's own packaging metadata promises that is not on disk, and a ``__pycache__`` whose sources are gone;
claims.why: The constants for staleness are defined, but the detection logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Derivable... the packaging gap in the other direction -- a package on disk that a wheel would not contain.
claims.why: No code for packaging gap detection appears in this chunk.

claims.text: NOT derivable... ``notes`` -- WHY a thing is the way it is. No scanner derives that.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes 'notes' and _strip_human removes it from the digest, consistent with notes being human-only.

claims.text: NOT derivable... ``kind`` -- the semantic taxonomy (safety / orchestration / provider / memory). A path prefix is a hint, not a fact.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes 'kind' and _strip_human removes it, consistent with kind being human-owned.

claims.text: NOT derivable... ``name`` -- the human-legible name of a capability, as opposed to the file it happens to live in.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes 'name' and _strip_human removes it, consistent with name being human-owned.

claims.text: NOT derivable... ``status: planned`` and ``status: baseline`` -- a feature that has no code yet has no evidence a scanner can read, and "this is deliberately only a baseline" is a judgement.
claims.why: No code for status handling appears in this chunk.

claims.text: NOT derivable... every feature whose surface is not Python: the web app, the VS Code extension, the crew protocol files. The reachability engine walks ``.py``; claiming to have measured a ``.tsx`` would be a lie of scope.
claims.why: No code for non-Python features appears in this chunk.

claims.text: THE MERGE: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run. Human fields live in ``annotations`` (keyed to a module, an env var or a route) and ``narrative_features`` (whole hand-written entries with no mechanical counterpart), and are merged into the output for consumers -- but the ``digest`` is computed over a projection that strips them again.
claims.why: _strip_human removes both 'annotations' and 'narrative_features' (via _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS) and _digest computes over that stripped projection.

claims.text: So: editing a note, a name or a kind is legal and does not trip the gate; editing a ``status``, a test list or an island entry DOES trip it, because that is the half a human is not supposed to write.
claims.why: _strip_human removes 'name', 'kind', 'notes' from features, so edits to those do not change the digest. Status and test lists are not in the human fields and would affect the digest.

claims.text: That is a refinement of the rule :func:`daedalus.mapping.drift._digest` states for the map snapshot, where the human half is a whole top-level block. Here the human half is interleaved with the mechanical half by field, so the digest is taken over a projection instead of over a key list.
claims.why: The comparison to drift._digest cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Annotations carry human fields ONLY. An annotation cannot set ``status`` and cannot add a module, because the failure being fixed is a hand-written file steering the work queue -- handing that same power back through a side door would be the same defect wearing a generated file's clothes.
claims.why: No annotation validation logic appears in this chunk.

claims.text: _strip_human: The mechanical projection of a whole document. Everything a human is allowed to write is removed: the human top-level blocks, and the human FIELDS interleaved into the generated records. What is left is exactly what this module derives, which is exactly what a digest should be a function of.
claims.why: The function removes _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS, FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS, AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS, ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS, and reduces repo_state to head only.

claims.text: _digest: A hash over the derived half only. Canonical JSON, sorted keys, so the value is a function of the content and not of the writer's key order.
claims.why: json.dumps uses sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), and the input is the stripped document.

claims.text: digest_ok: Does this document's own digest still cover its own derived fields? Public for the same reason :func:`daedalus.mapping.drift.digest_ok` is: any consumer that RANKS WORK out of these lists rather than rescanning has to ask this first. Ranking work out of a hand-edited census is precisely the defect this module was written to end.
claims.why: The function returns False for non-mappings or docs with __error__, then compares stored digest to _digest(doc).

claims.text: _pyproject_packages: The explicit ``[tool.setuptools] packages`` list, or ``[]``. A line scanner rather than a TOML parser: this module is stdlib-only across 3.10 (no ``tomllib``), and the shape being read is one array under one known table. An unreadable or absent pyproject yields an empty list, which both detectors below read as "no promise was made" -- never as a finding.
claims.why: The function body is truncated at the end of the chunk; the actual reading logic and error handling are not visible.

claims.text: STATUS_BY_CLASS: ``orphan`` folds into ``island``: both mean "no entry point reaches it", and the map's own gate already merges them (drift.ISLAND_CLASSES). ``test`` modules are not features and are dropped entirely.
claims.why: The mapping shows 'orphan': 'island'. The dropping of 'test' modules is not visible here but the comment is consistent with the mapping.

claims.text: _STALE_SKIP_DIRS: Deliberately NOT the same set as reach._IGNORE_DIRS: ``build`` and ``__pycache__`` are excluded there precisely because they are not source, and they are exactly what this sweep is looking for.
claims.why: The comment references reach._IGNORE_DIRS which is not in this chunk; the set itself is defined but the comparison cannot be verified.

claims.text: _METHOD_BY_SUFFIX: The HTTP method a route handler implies. web_api dispatches on the request method by putting it in the handler's name, so this is a reading of the evidence rather than a guess -- and a handler that does not follow the convention yields "" rather than a fabricated method.
claims.why: _method_of returns '' if no suffix matches, and the suffixes are defined in _METHOD_BY_SUFFIX.

claims.text: _TOKEN_RE: Starts at a letter or underscore so "/api/x" and ".claude/y" do not produce a phantom leading-punctuation token.
claims.why: The regex pattern starts with [A-Za-z_], which prevents matches starting with punctuation.

claims.text: _strip_human: repo_state: The revision, and only the revision. ``branch`` and ``dirty`` move without the architecture moving, and a gate that goes red because somebody has unsaved edits is a gate people switch off.
claims.why: The code sets body['repo_state'] = {'head': state.get('head')}, discarding branch and dirty.

observations.what: The chunk defines many constants and functions but the majority of the module's logic (harvest, build, check, etc.) is in later chunks. Claims about derivation and merge cannot be fully verified from this chunk.
_strip_human excludes 'annotations' and 'narrative_features' from the digest, but the docstring claims they are merged into the output. The merge logic is not in this chunk.
The regex _TOKEN_RE allows backslashes and dots, which could match Windows paths or dotted names. The comment only mentions leading punctuation.
